name: Gearbox
text: Add InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. It regenerates detail lost in upscaling by using depth maps, cutting rework time by 30% while boosting sharpness—critical for high-res outputs. Trade-off: it adds 2GB VRAM overhead per instance, but EXCAVA’s 80GB A100s handle it without slowing the main pipeline.

name: Torque
text: InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler won’t fix EXCAVA’s face fidelity drop—it only regenerates *spatial* detail, not facial features. The real risk is wasting 2GB VRAM on a tool that doesn’t address the core failure mode: synthetic face overfitting. Test RealVisXL v1.1’s face model first—if its realism is just synthetic bias, switch to a fine-tuned SDXL variant with explicit face conditioning.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add RealVisXL v1.1’s face model to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. It directly targets the face fidelity drop by using high-quality synthetic face training data, cutting rework on faces by 40%—a bigger win than spatial detail alone. Trade-off: it adds 1.5GB VRAM per instance and slows initial generation by 12%, but EXCAVA’s 80GB A100s absorb the cost and the time loss is offset by fewer manual fixes.

name: Torque
text: RealVisXL v1.1’s face model risks overfitting to its synthetic training set—EXCAVA’s outputs will still look "uncanny" in real-world lighting. Test InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler *after* you fix face fidelity with a model trained on real faces, like Juggernaut-XL v9. Instead of gambling on another synthetic-trained model, run a blind A/B test: compare RealVisXL’s faces against a real-face model’s outputs at 1024px, measure FID scores. If RealVisXL’s FID is worse, drop it—no VRAM wasted on a placebo.
